fields.meta_title: Solar Landing Page for Installer Quotes | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A solar landing page that reads usage off a bill photo and routes the request. See four installer examples, from batteries to repairs. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Solar Landing Page That Reads the Electric Bill
fields.hero_description: Build a solar landing page that turns a photo of an electric bill into a quote request, saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Sits Between the Ad and the Site Visit
fields.features_subheading: A solar landing page earns a request from a homeowner with a bill in hand. Emergent builds these six parts from your prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A bill photo, not a guess at usage

Ask homeowners to upload their latest electric bill, not type a monthly figure. The app pulls the usage and the billing month off the photo, and a person checks any unclear value.
fields.feature_2:
Two roof questions, and no more

Ask which way the main roof faces and how much of it trees shade at midday. Leave pitch, age, and material off the form and check them in person during the site visit.
fields.feature_3:
A page for each job you sell

Give rooftop quotes, battery storage, business systems, and repairs a page each. An ad for battery backup then lands on questions about the panels already installed, not the roof.
fields.feature_4:
An email to whoever owns the job

Name in your prompt who handles each kind of request. The app emails that person each new request with the answers the visitor gave, and sends every other request to the office.
fields.feature_5:
Requests kept as rows you can sort

Every request saves as a row with the job type, the answers it carried, and the ad it came from. Sort a season of quotes by job type or by ad campaign, in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
The page and its code, yours to move

Export the page, its forms, and the request table to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Or keep the page hosted on Emergent, under your own domain name, which uses credits.

fields.usecase_heading: Solar Landing Page Examples by Job
fields.tab_content_1:
One bill photo, one kWh figure on the quote

Sunhallow Solar's quote page skips the usage question and asks for a photo of the latest electric bill. The app reads the kWh used and the billing month into the request, and any reading it is unsure of goes to Wenna Strathe to check. This week 48 bills came in: 41 read cleanly and 7 went to Wenna.
fields.tab_content_2:
With whole home backup, a designer calls

Pennant Energy's battery page is for owners who already have panels. It asks for the system size in kW, then Whole home or Essentials only. Whole home requests go to Ravi Kalloo, the storage designer. Everything else goes to the sales team. This month 27 battery requests came in: 11 for Ravi and 16 for sales.
fields.tab_content_3:
For a farm building, a ground-mount designer reads first

Thistlebrook Solar asks business owners for the building type and the average monthly electric bill. Farm building requests go to Gaelen Moberg, who designs ground-mount arrays, and the rest go to the commercial team. This quarter 18 requests came in: 8 warehouses, 6 offices, and 4 farm buildings.
fields.tab_content_4:
A fault light on the inverter means an email to Petra

Cardinal Ridge Solar Service asks for the symptom first, such as Inverter fault light, then the address and the system size. A fault light request emails Petra Lindell, the technician on call. This week 9 of 15 repair requests named the fault light, and 6 went to the queue.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Solar Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a solar landing page that reads usage from a bill photo and sends each request to the person who handles it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every ad you plan to run
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Make the bill upload the first field
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each ad and the job it sells. A battery ad and a rooftop ad call for different questions, so give each job a page of its own, and the form will match the promise in the ad that brought the visitor there.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the form with the bill upload. The usage printed on a bill is a better start for a quote than a figure recalled from memory, and the homeowner needs nothing more than a phone camera to send it from the kitchen table.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put the address and the phone number after the bill and the roof questions, so the first screen asks about the house, not the person. Mark only the fields the designer needs before a visit as required, and leave the rest optional.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put photos of systems your crews finished beside the form, each captioned with the town and the system size in kW. Use your own installs on local streets in place of stock photos of panels at sunset.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Say who calls back, and when
fields.howto_step_5_des: Under the button, state who follows up and by when, such as a call by the next business day. Promise only what the office can keep every week of the year, and put the phone number beside the button for a homeowner who prefers to call.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Name the person for each job
fields.howto_step_6_des: List each job in your prompt with the person who takes it: battery requests to the storage designer, farm buildings to the ground-mount designer, inverter faults to the technician on call. Emergent writes those rules into the page and its emails.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Upload one of your own bills
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the first ad runs, upload a bill of your own from a phone and send one request of each kind. Check that the usage was read right, that each email reached its person, and that every test shows up as a row in the table.

faq_plan.q: What is a solar landing page?
faq_plan.a: A solar landing page is one page built for one solar offer, such as a rooftop quote or a battery for an existing system. It ends in a single action, usually a quote request, carries no site menu to wander off through, and every ad for that offer points to it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a solar landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder in plain English: the offer, the questions the form asks, and who gets each request. Emergent builds the page and the table each request saves to. Test the bill upload from your own phone before the ads go live.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a solar landing page ask homeowners?
faq_plan.a: Ask for five things and stop there: a photo of the bill, the roof direction, the shade on it, the address, and a phone number. Everything else can wait for the site visit. Forms built with Emergent take requests with no response cap.

faq_plan.q: Should a solar landing page show a price?
faq_plan.a: Show a price only if your office will honor it before anyone has seen the roof. A cleaning service landing page can price a job from a room count. A solar page that cannot do that should say the price comes after the site visit, and list what the written quote will include.

faq_plan.q: Why ask for an electric bill on a solar landing page?
faq_plan.a: It gives the designer real usage in kWh instead of a figure the homeowner has to guess. Ask for the latest bill, and add an optional second upload for a summer bill if your crews quote homes that run air conditioning. Emergent builds the upload and the fields it fills from your prompt.

faq_plan.q: Should battery storage get its own solar landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you sell batteries to owners who already have panels. Their form asks about the system they own, such as its size in kW, and skips the roof questions. Point battery ads at that page and keep the rooftop quote page for new installs.

faq_plan.q: How is a solar landing page different from a solar company website?
faq_plan.a: The website answers every question about the company. The landing page asks for one thing, the quote request, and has no menu to pull the visitor away from it. Point each ad at its own page. A landscaping landing page splits off a seasonal offer the same way.

faq_plan.q: How do I see which ads bring requests to my solar landing page?
faq_plan.a: Tag each ad's link with a campaign name, and have the page save that tag with every request. Count requests by campaign each week and pause any ad whose clicks bring none. The requests live in a database you own, and you can count them any way you like.

faq_plan.q: Can a solar landing page book the site visit too?
faq_plan.a: Yes. After the quote request, show the open site visit days for the next two weeks and let the homeowner pick one. The booking saves with the request. The designer then arrives with the bill already read and the roof answers in hand.

faq_plan.q: What should a solar landing page say after someone sends a request?
faq_plan.a: Thank the homeowner by name, say who will call and by when, and list what that call covers: the usage read from the bill and the roof answers. A plumber landing page confirms an urgent job the same way, with the time the plumber is expected at the door.

plan.angle: Searches for solar landing page return template galleries and lead-generation agency posts that show a solar page's layout, never what the form asks or where a request goes after the homeowner taps the button. This page shows four installer pages built around that hand-off (a rooftop quote form that reads usage from a photo of the electric bill, a battery storage page that splits whole home backup from essentials, a business rooftop page sorted by building type with farms sent to the ground-mount designer, a repair page that emails inverter faults to a technician), each with the form, the routing and the saved row, then the build steps an installer needs. It makes no tax credit, incentive, net metering, savings, panel output or state-specific claims. Roofing, HVAC, electrician and contractor pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

specificity.evidence: Installer vocabulary throughout: 'kWh used and the billing month', 'Whole home or Essentials only', 'ground-mount arrays', 'Inverter fault light'.

voice.evidence: Plain verbs and unglamorous detail ('48 bills came in: 41 read cleanly and 7 went to Wenna'); bolted-on sibling-link sentences recorded as a note.

findings.issue: An 'every' claim false for the page's own examples (rework-checklist 7): the battery page skips the roof questions (feature_3 'not the roof', FAQ 6 'skips the roof questions'), the business page asks for an average monthly bill in dollars, not kWh, and the repair page asks for symptom, address and system size with no kWh or roof answers.
